chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Two men do not inherit from each other when one of them has killed his companion.
ai.seo_question: Does a murderer inherit from the person they killed according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *shighbah* (hindrance), where a murderer is legally barred from inheriting from their victim. This ruling, derived from the Prophet's practice and affirmed by the Imams, prevents the killer from profiting from their crime, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence and distinct from general inheritance laws.
